source.title: Modality-Aware SAM: Sharpness-Aware-Minimization Driven Gradient Modulation for Harmonized Multimodal Learning
source.authors: Hossein R. Nowdeh; Jie Ji; Xiao-Long Ma; Fatemeh Afghah

record.tranche_reason: Extends sharpness and generalization-gap analysis to multimodal learning, reporting normalized overfitting-gap curves and loss-landscape comparisons for several training methods.
record.gate_note: Figure 2 reports normalized overfitting-gap curves on AV-MNIST for five methods and three modality views. Figures 1 and 2 are described as showing flatter landscapes and smaller gaps for M-SAM. The paper does not measure magnitude-aware perturbation sharpness or compare its ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.
record.test_reason: The study uses the flat-minima rationale to design M-SAM and evaluates its multimodal classification performance. It does not measure V7's magnitude-scaled perturbation tolerance or independently test its association with generalization gaps. None of V1–V8 is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes the authors' conclusion: M-SAM promotes flatter optima and improves overall multimodal performance across four benchmarks. This should not be read as superiority on every modality-specific accuracy measure; the authors explicitly acknowledge lower single-modality accuracies in some comparisons.
record.recipe_differences: The study proposes a modality-aware SAM optimizer for multimodal learning and evaluates it against other methods; it does not reproduce the magnitude-aware sharpness measurement in V7.
record.method_sensitivity: Fusion strategy (early or late), dataset, and modality view are varied in the reported experiments.

fits_no_version.finding: Figure 2 compares normalized absolute training–test accuracy gaps across five methods and three modality views on AV-MNIST with late fusion. The authors describe M-SAM as maintaining closely matched training and validation accuracy.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: M-SAM reduces normalized overfitting gaps in the tested multimodal training setting.

fits_no_version.finding: Figure 1 qualitatively compares CREMA-D late-fusion loss landscapes for AGM, SAM, and M-SAM; the authors describe M-SAM's landscape as flatter. No magnitude-scaled perturbation-tolerance measurement is reported.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: M-SAM produces visually flatter loss landscapes than the compared methods on CREMA-D.

fits_no_version.finding: Tables 1 and 2 report multimodal and modality-specific accuracy for optimizer and gradient-modulation methods across four datasets and two fusion strategies.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: M-SAM improves overall multimodal classification accuracy over the tested baselines.

record.problems: The gap comparisons in Figure 2 are figure-only; no numerical values or uncertainty estimates are reported in the supplied text. The paper does not directly measure magnitude-aware sharpness.
record.rows_left_out: No rows retained: the plotted normalized overfitting-gap results do not measure the magnitude-aware sharpness named by V7, and the remaining claim versions are not tested.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and its comparison with natural-label held-out accuracy.
Test error as width increases beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected networks and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under limited and broader tuning.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and compensating recipe changes.
Dropout effects and their dependence on training-set size, configuration, and augmentation.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance, its association with generalization gaps among similarly fitted networks, and its ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.
Test-accuracy effects of removing highly memorized versus random training examples.

record.verdict_notes: Correct the record's T3 classification and V7 tested_not_extracted status. The normalized accuracy gap is treated as a sharpness proxy rather than paired with an independent magnitude-aware sharpness measurement. The gap curves and landscape visualizations also concern different datasets. These results do not establish or challenge V7, and their omission from claim-linked rows is appropriate.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label test performance.
Width sweep beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected architecture comparisons.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under the specified tuning regimes.
Large-batch versus small-batch performance under fixed epoch budgets.

The study reports overfitting-gap curves and loss-landscape visualizations, but does not test magnitude-aware, weight-scaled perturbation sharpness or its ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing memorized examples and measuring the resulting test-accuracy change.
